items.title: HERD: Harness-Evolving Recursive Distillation for Continual Learning
items.summary_1line: Continual learning requires a model to keep acquiring new skills and knowledge without compromising its existing capabilities. Parametric methods suffer from catastrophic forgetting and loss of plasticity. Non-paramet...
items.editor_note: Frames the problem: parametric forgetting versus non-parametric limits, with a distillation approach.

items.title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
items.summary_1line: Continual learning is the ability of LLM agents to improve over time by acquiring, refining, and applying knowledge from experience while retaining useful prior knowledge. It is essential for agents learning over long...
items.why_it_matters: Matches feed focus: agent, harness, evaluation.
items.editor_note: Adds a benchmark for agents learning from experience over long horizons.

items.title: CAMR: Compatibility-Aware Memory Replay for Continual Learning in Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: Continual learning requires large language models to acquire new knowledge and capabilities while retaining what they have learned. Fine-tuning and replay support acquisition and retention, but deciding whether incomi...
items.editor_note: Adds a replay-selection method that judges whether new data is compatible before use.

items.title: Routed Continual Learning
items.summary_1line: Agents deployed at scale repeatedly encounter related problems, and it is natural to let them learn from each other's experience rather than starting over each time. Unfortunately, there is no single way to retain tha...
items.editor_note: Extends the question to agents at scale learning from each other's experience.

editorial.tldr: An Oct 22 paper (HERD) framed continual learning as a trade-off between parametric methods, which forget, and non-parametric ones. A benchmark followed on Oct 25 for whether LLM agents improve from experience, then CAMR on Oct 27 for choosing what to replay.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 28: Routed Continual Learning lets deployed agents share experience, routing among retention mechanisms rather than relying on a single one.
editorial.why_it_matters: Agents that learn from experience need retention without regressions; replay selection, long-horizon evals and now cross-agent sharing are the pieces to watch.
editorial.take_for_builders: Treat these as research signals: do not adopt, but add a retention check to any fine-tune or agent-memory pipeline that updates on new data.

status.detail: Four arXiv papers in seven days; all research-stage, none shipped in a product.
